Just as the characteristic of bodhi is pure by its very nature, all dharmas likewise possess this same characteristic; this is what is termed the sacred true dharma of the noble ones.
Subhūti said: "Good son! There are four noble truths which are called the true truths."
"What are the four?
They are the truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path.
Thus spoke the Bodhisattva Asamudācāra.
“Venerable Subhūti! Do you not say that suffering is conditioned? Subhūti replied:
"In this way, son of good family!
I have always taught that suffering is a conditioned phenomenon (*saṃskṛtadharma*). The Bodhisattva Anutpāda said:
"Venerable Subhūti! The Tathāgata has always taught that all conditioned phenomena are false. Subhūti replied:
"In this way, son of good family,
the Tathāgata has always taught that all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta-dharma*) are entirely false.
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda said:
"If that is so, why do you say that suffering is a true reality?
Venerable Subhūti! If one says that suffering is a conditioned phenomenon (*saṃskṛtadharma*), then it is false."
Subhūti said: "Good son! Suffering is conditioned, false, and unreal."
"I say that the knowledge of suffering is taken as the ultimate truth.
The Bodhisattva Asaṃpramoṣa said: "Subhūti!..."
"If suffering is conditioned, illusory, and unreal, then the wisdom that knows that suffering must also be illusory and not real. Subhūti said:
"O son of good family!"
"In this way, in this way, even the knowledge that knows suffering is likewise illusory.
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda said, "Venerable Subhūti!"
"If it is thus, how does one know that 'suffering is a noble truth' through wisdom? Subhūti replied,
"O son of good family!..."
"The Truth of Cessation is an unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*). If that is so, why is it not a Noble Truth (*āryasatya*)?
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda replied:
“Venerable Subhūti! By the cessation of what phenomena is it called the Truth of Cessation?
Is it called ‘cessation’ because those phenomena cease of their own accord?”
"Is there anything further that is extinguished which is called 'extinction'? Subhūti replied,
"O son of good family!"
The Proponent of Conditioned Phenomena said, "The cessation of all sufferings is called the Truth of Cessation.
Bodhisattva Asamudācāra said, "Subhūti!..."
"Do you not say that suffering is conditioned, illusory, and unreal? Subhūti replied, "It is so, noble son!"
I said to him: "Suffering is a conditioned phenomenon; it is false and unreal.
The Bodhisattva Asamudgata said:
“Venerable Subhūti! If dharmas are illusory and unreal, then those dharmas have no cessation.
If this is so, why do you say that the complete extinction of all suffering is called the Truth of Cessation?”
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Anutpāda, saying:
"Noble son! I give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward such unimpeded eloquence of yours, Great Being."
“O son of good family!
May all sentient beings attain such eloquence. Subhūti said:
“Good son! What is the realized wisdom of the true reality of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda replied:
“Subhūti! All dharmas do not contradict the practice of the ultimate truth; therefore, to realize all dharmas is called realizing the ultimate truth. Subhūti!”
All phenomena arise from causes and conditions; to know these dependently arisen phenomena as they truly are is called the True Reality (*satya*).
To know all phenomena as empty as they truly are is called the True Reality; one who realizes emptiness is said to realize the True Reality.
All phenomena are non-arising; to realize that all phenomena are non-arising is called realizing the True Reality.
Subhūti, whatever dharma one realizes as the ultimate truth, within that dharma there is not even a single dharma to be grasped or a single dharma to be abandoned. Subhūti!
This is called the realization of true knowledge by all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Subhūti, that which is called the "ultimate truth" is the proclamation of the dharma of non-conceptualization.
Why is this? Subhūti! All that is conceptualized is false dharma.
Subhūti! As for what you have just said:
"The Great Being has attained a most excellent benefit; having received the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, he will certainly attain Buddhahood."
"Subhūti! If a person considers themselves to have quickly attained a great benefit, the Buddha does not bestow a prediction of enlightenment upon that person;
if a person remains free from such a sense of having quickly attained a great benefit, it is such a person as the Buddha bestows a prediction of enlightenment."
If a person does not give rise to joy upon gaining gain and offerings, nor feels distress upon losing them, this person is given a prediction of enlightenment;
if a person attains nirvana without departing from the world, this person is given a prediction of enlightenment;
if a person realizes the noble path without abandoning ordinary dharmas, this person is given a prediction of enlightenment.
"If a person hears the prophecy and does not rejoice, that person has received the prophecy. Subhūti said: "Good son!..."
"If that which is directed toward and that which is known are understood in this way, their meaning is profoundly deep.
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda said: "Subhūti!..."
“If a person does not perceive coming or going, that person knows the profound.
Subhūti said, “This profound Dharma is difficult to understand.”
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda said:
“Subhūti! If a person wishes to see this profound [reality], that person will not be able to see it.”
Subhūti said: "One who knows in this way is difficult to comprehend.
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda said:
“Subhūti! One who does not practice is also difficult to understand. Subhūti said:
“Good son! What kind of sentient beings are able to give rise to faith in the profound Dharma?
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda replied:
“Subhūti! If a person has already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas of the past, that person will be able to believe. Subhūti!”
If a person is unable to plant various roots of goodness and does not practice the cultivation of making offerings to the Buddhas, such a person will ultimately be unable to hear this Dharma-gate.
Subhūti said: "Good son! How does one come to make offerings to all the Buddhas?"
The Bodhisattva Asaṃprasthita said:
"If a person can abide in practice according to reality, that person is said to be making offerings to all Buddhas. Subhūti said:
“Good son! How can one abide in practice according to reality?
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda replied:
"If a person can resolve their mind to practice for the sake of all sentient beings.
Subhūti asked: "In what way does one resolve their mind to practice for the sake of all sentient beings?"
The Bodhisattva Asaṃprasthita said,
"If one can not abandon great loving-kindness and great compassion. Subhūti said:
"What is called the great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) of a bodhisattva?
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda replied:

"If a bodhisattva is able to relinquish their own body, life, and all roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) to give them to sentient beings without seeking any recompense, this is called great loving-kindness."
Subhūti asked: “What is called the great compassion of a bodhisattva?
The Bodhisattva Anutpāda replied:
"If a bodhisattva first bestows unsurpassed bodhi upon sentient beings and only afterwards realizes it for themselves, this is called great compassion.

When this profound Dharma gate was being taught, seventy-six thousand sentient beings resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and two hundred bhikṣus, having become free from all outflows (āsrava), attained liberation of mind.
At that time, there was a son of heaven in the assembly named Suvicintin, who addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
How does a bodhisattva abide in the fundamental sphere of practice for the enlightenment of a Buddha?"
The Buddha said:
"Devaputra! If a bodhisattva can accomplish a profound and upright mind and give rise to the unsurpassed resolve, this is called the fundamental dwelling place of bodhi."
The Devaputra Sucintita said:
“For those bodhisattvas who have thus resolved their minds, what dharma serves as their objective sphere?
The Buddha said:
"If one can practice the sphere of generosity without seeking the gate of requital or reward;
if one can practice the sphere of ethical discipline without discriminating between the gates of maintaining ethical conduct;
if one can practice the sphere of patience without perceiving the gate of the exhaustion and cessation of phenomena; if one can practice the sphere of diligence..."
Not initiating the gateway of practice and so forth, yet constantly practicing within the realm of dhyāna while being able to directly perceive all dharma-gateways;
practicing within the realm of prajñā while not seeing that gateway of non-conceptualization manifest before one;
constantly seeking the realm of śruta-mayī-prajñā while not seeing the gateway of verbal expressions and the like manifest before one; practicing śamatha...
The gateway of seeing that all phenomena are primordially pure and quiescent by transcending their objective domains;
the gateway of the manifestation of the non-perception of all phenomena through the cultivation of the domain of vipaśyanā;

the gateway of the manifestation of non-recollection and non-mental-construction through the cultivation of the domain of the four foundations of mindfulness; and the cultivation of the domain of the four right efforts...
The gateway of non-action manifests before them; the gateway of severing all vows and desires manifests while practicing the sphere of the four bases of psychic power;
the gateway of transcending all faculties manifests while practicing the sphere of the five faculties;
the gateway of non-destruction manifests while practicing the sphere of the five powers; and they practice the seven factors of enlightenment.
The realm of the gateway to the Buddha’s bodhi manifests before one; the realm of practicing the Eightfold Noble Path manifests for the sake of rescuing sentient beings who travel on wrong paths;
the realm of practicing the teaching and transformation of sentient beings manifests as the dharma-gate of no sentient beings and no dharma of deliverance;
and the realm of practicing the severing of afflictions manifests as the vision that the intrinsic nature of all dharmas is detached.
While the gateway of afflictions manifests before them, they practice the realms of the various *pāramitās* without clinging to this shore or the other shore;
while practicing the realms of the mundane world, the gateway of *nirvāṇa* manifests before them;
while practicing the realm of *nirvāṇa*, the gateway of performing all conditioned activities (*saṃskāra*) manifests before them; and while practicing the realm of birth, they do not take birth.
The gate of non-extinction manifests; the gate of practicing the realm of the aggregates while remaining free from afflictions manifests;
the gate of non-differentiation manifests while practicing the realm of the elements; the gate of entering the noble path manifests while practicing the realm of the sense bases;
and the gate of tranquil meditative concentration manifests while practicing the realm of hearing the Dharma.

While practicing the sphere of preaching the Dharma, the gate of non-discourse manifests before them; while practicing the accomplishment of the sphere of physical forms, the gate of the Dharma-body manifests before them;
while practicing the sphere of turning the wheel of Dharma, the gate of neither turning nor speaking manifests before them;
while practicing the sphere of the śrāvakas, the gates of all Buddha-dharmas manifest before them; while practicing...
“While practicing within the realm of the pratyekabuddhas, the gateways of the superior practices of all bodhisattvas manifest before them, O Devaputra!
This is called the realm of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
The Devaputra Subhāvitacitta addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is called the practice of all bodhisattvas?
The Buddha said:
“Devaputra! You have renounced your own pleasure and are able to bestow happiness upon all sentient beings;
though you constantly dwell in the world, you maintain the precepts and are widely learned, with a mind free from negligence.”
Constantly abiding in nirvana yet not abandoning great compassion, the gateway to nirvana is manifest before them yet they do not seek its realization.
For the sake of transforming sentient beings, they act in accordance with the ways of the world to protect all beings.

They are able to maintain an impartial mind toward all sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to attain a pure mind; they harbor no discrimination in their hearts toward any sentient being and share all things with everyone.

He preaches the Dharma for the sake of others, not for the sake of food or drink; he maintains pure requisites and is always content; he constantly delights in secluded places, reflecting with right mindfulness; and he always dwells among the great assembly, preaching the Dharma without weariness.
Entering cities and villages, they manifest compassion; they do not seek praise, offerings, or respect, and are always able to remain far removed from worldly idle chatter.

In all their speech, they do not contravene the Buddha-dharma; they are appropriately concise or detailed, speak with affection and gentleness, pay homage to the Triple Gem with every part of their body, and take the initiative to offer greetings.
The mind always delights in the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya); the mind has no attachment to any phenomena (dharma), and the mind does not crave or become defiled by the necessities of life.
One should constantly associate with sages and remain far removed from what is contrary to the Dharma.
One should love the Dharma as one’s own body and revere the Buddha as one’s own life; one should cherish and respect spiritual practice as one cherishes one’s head and torso.

Regarding all matters of clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and the necessities of life, one should be content with what little is obtained. One should honor and respect one’s teachers and elders as if they were the World-Honored One, and even at the cost of losing one’s own body and life, never abandon the Bodhicitta.
During the first and last watches of the night, he practiced with diligent effort; meditative concentration and samādhi were constantly present before him.
He contemplated and correctly observed the Dharma as he had heard it, seeking liberation through subtle wisdom.
If one cultivates a pure mind free from defilement and turbidity, one is able to relinquish all possessions; one contemplates the internal body and does not follow after external forms.
One can renounce what is given, remain far removed from anger, extinguish ignorance, and increase *prajñā*.
They are able to guard the precepts and do not deviate from their practice.
In all circumstances they give rise to a supple mind; in all circumstances they take wisdom as their foremost priority, possessing a non-perverted mind and stainless radiance.
With a mind that constantly cultivates the various pāramitās, with a mind that does not abandon diligence, and always seeking roots of goodness;
they do not forget the Dharma as it was heard, and they explain the Dharma as it was heard to others.

Free from thoughts of offerings, food, drink, and the like; always guarding the sense faculties; always maintaining a mind in meditative concentration; always following a mind inclined toward nirvana; and never abandoning the mind that remains within the world—such a person cannot be moved by gain or loss, profit or decline, defamation or praise, fame or insignificance, nor by suffering or pleasure.
"In all circumstances, one should give rise to this thought:

'Through giving, one attains great wealth; through upholding the precepts, one is born among gods or humans; through patience, one attains physical beauty; through diligence, one abandons afflictions;
through meditative concentration (*samādhi*), one attains pliancy of mind; and by cultivating wisdom (*prajñā*), one comes to know the world.'"
Practicing the mundane and supramundane dharmas; practicing the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) without any faults;
practicing the four immeasurable minds (*apramāṇa*) without arrogance; practicing the wisdom of truth, relinquishment, cessation, and insight to attain tranquility and pliancy;
practicing meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) to attain a mind of mastery; cultivating samādhi to attain a profound mind; and practicing the truths as they truly are.
Truly knowing all phenomena, they practice meditative concentration while remaining detached from all views; practicing the signless, they attain non-conceptuality;
practicing the wishless, they attain a mind free from attachment; practicing the various *pāramitās*, they attain the ultimate Mahāyāna mind;
and practicing the *upāya-pāramitā*, they attain the station of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*). Thus they practice.
Practicing the ten stages of the bodhisattva to fulfill all bodhisattva deeds; drawing near to spiritual friends to attain the gateway to all merits;
revering and obeying preceptors and acharyas to be able to accord with all Buddhas;
knowing one's own mind to attain the knowledge of all modes; practicing without arrogance to attain great majestic power; and being respectful...
By reverently prostrating to all sentient beings, one attains the state where no sentient being can see the crown of one's head;
by practicing various forms of giving, one attains a body endowed with the excellent primary marks; by complying with all sentient beings, one attains the eighty minor marks;
by expounding the Mahāyāna Dharma, one attains the stage of mastery; and by teaching sentient beings to resolve upon Bodhicitta, one attains...
The stage of non-retrogression; preaching the emptiness of all phenomena to sever afflictions and the habitual tendencies of afflictions;

attaining the four analytical knowledges through the gift of Dharma; attaining dhāraṇīs by inspiring mindfulness in sentient beings; causing sentient beings to know the Dharma so they attain the four analytical knowledges;
attaining the unerring power of recollection through the cause of providing joy in eloquent exposition to sentient beings; [and acting] toward those who are weak and inferior...
By giving rise to the mind of patience toward sentient beings, one attains the body of Nārāyaṇa;

by giving rise to the mind of patience toward sentient beings who violate the precepts, one attains a mind that is revered by all who see them; by being able to extinguish the mind of resentment, sentient beings attain a mind of constant concentration;
by diligently practicing vigor, they swiftly realize the practice of the Dharma; and through samādhi, they bestow [benefit] upon all sentient beings.
He is born with the mark of the secret organ being concealed; through his majestic deportment, he accomplishes all matters of universal adornment;
he causes sentient beings to draw near to spiritual friends so that Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas are always present before them;
having abandoned thoughts of desire, he is constantly trusted by all the world; and having abandoned thoughts of anger...
He attains that which is beloved by all the world; he abandons stinginess and envy to attain all renown and gain;
he is able to act as a place of reliance for sentient beings to attain the refuge of all the world;
he abandons all offerings, honor, and praise to attain the food of Dharma-joy and a beautiful reputation; he is the first to give.
By inquiring after others' well-being, one obtains pure speech; by giving kind words, one obtains the Brahma-voice;
by giving gentle speech, one obtains the voice of the kalaviṅka bird; by remaining free from anger and resentment, one obtains a body of supreme excellence among all the worlds;
by not deceiving sentient beings, one becomes trusted by all the world; by not speaking of the faults of others, one obtains...
By not entering the womb, one attains immeasurable life free from killing; by abstaining from theft, one obtains a treasury as vast as space;
by relinquishing beloved things, one attains a hand that holds wish-fulfilling jewels; by dedicating merit toward Bodhi, one obtains inexhaustible wealth;
by abstaining from sexual misconduct, one attains the body of a Great Man; by abstaining from falsehood...
By attaining secrecy in the karma of speech, one distances oneself from divisive talk and does not lose the bodhicitta;
by distancing oneself from harsh speech, one gains the praise of all the world; by distancing oneself from frivolous speech, one gains an indestructible retinue;
by distancing oneself from covetousness, one gains an inexhaustible treasury; and by distancing oneself from anger, one becomes a benefactor for all sentient beings.
By constructing bridges, one abandons wrong views and attains right view; by teaching and transforming sentient beings, one dwells in the Mahāyāna and attains the ten powers of a Buddha;
by being able to give everything without seeking karmic retribution, one attains the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
and by relinquishing all attachments, one attains the four fearlessnesses.
“O Son of Heaven!

If I were to explain at length such infinite realms of bodhisattvas and the infinite practices of bodhisattvas, even in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, I could not reach their end.”
"O Devaputra!
This is called the bodhisattva’s sphere of practice.
O Devaputra!"
"If a bodhisattva thus accomplishes the sphere of activity and thus practices, the attainment of enlightenment will not be difficult.
The Devaputra Sucintita said:
"World-Honored One!"
"How is it that a bodhisattva is called 'peaceful and secure'?
The Buddha said,
"O Son of Heaven!..."
If a bodhisattva never abandons samādhi, yet does not take birth based upon that samādhi,
then having attained samādhi, they are born in whatever various places there may be where it is beneficial for sentient beings.
"O Son of Heaven!
A bodhisattva such as this is said to be 'secure.
Thus spoke the Devaputra Subhāvitacitta.
“World-Honored One!
In what way is a bodhisattva said to be ‘quiescent’?
The Buddha said:
“O Son of Heaven!
If a bodhisattva perceives all suchness, the dharma-realm, and the limit of reality, this bodhisattva is able to remain tranquil while dwelling amidst the great assembly.
It should be known thus, O Son of Heaven!”
This, O Devaputra, is called the tranquility of a bodhisattva.
If a bodhisattva does not give rise to a mind directed toward two locations, this is called the tranquility of a bodhisattva.
The devaputra said:
“World-Honored One,
how is it that a bodhisattva is said to be constantly in samādhi?”
The Buddha said, "Devaputra!

If a bodhisattva’s mind never seeks after any phenomena, does not perceive a single dharma that can be grasped, and does not perceive a single dharma that can be abandoned, then this bodhisattva, according to whatever dharmas he perceives, knows them all to be empty and quiescent, devoid of any reality."
"O Devaputra!
A Bodhisattva who is thus is said to be 'constantly in samādhi.
The Devaputra Subhāvitacitta said:
“World-Honored One!
How is it that a bodhisattva is said to have ‘reached all places’?
The Buddha said:
“Devaputra! If a bodhisattva can perceive that his own self and all sentient beings are equal, empty, and quiescent, Devaputra!
A bodhisattva such as this is said to have reached all places.”
The Devaputra Sucintita said:
“World-Honored One,
in what way is a bodhisattva said to be ‘tamed’?”
The Buddha said,
“Devaputra! If a bodhisattva cannot be moved by any conceptual discrimination, this is called being tamed.”
The devaputra asked,
"In what way is a bodhisattva said to have attained cessation?
The Buddha replied:
“If a bodhisattva is neither defiled nor pure, this is called attaining cessation.
The Devaputra Subhāvitacitta said:
“World-Honored One!
"As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, one attains bodhi by relying upon one's own mind.
World-Honored One!
In this way, a bodhisattva is free from all afflictions; in this very way, they take up the Buddha-dharma."
World-Honored One!
The dharmas of all Buddhas come from nowhere and go nowhere.
World-Honored One!
“The pure wisdom regarding all phenomena is called bodhi. O Devaputra!
When a bodhisattva thus accords with patience, it is called bodhi.”
"One who can know in this way is called an Omniscient One.
"World-Honored One!
If one can enter such an equal dharma-realm, that bodhisattva is said to have accomplished the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā)."
If one can thus know and achieve the realization of the equal dharma-realm, this bodhisattva is said to have accomplished the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā);
if one can thus know and endure the equal dharma-realm, it is called accomplishing the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā);
if one can practice the wisdoms of hearing, reflection, cultivation, and meditation within this dharma-gate, it is called accomplishing the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā).
If one can contemplate this Dharma as the equal dharma-realm, it is called the accomplishment of the dhyāna-pāramitā;
if one can thoroughly comprehend such a Dharma as the equal dharma-realm, it is called the prajñā-pāramitā.
"Bhagavān! If there is a person who can believe in this dharma-gate, that person is said to have seen the Dharma, is said to have realized the Dharma, and is said to have subdued Māra. Bhagavān!"
If a person can expound this Dharma-gate, that person will be able to turn in accordance with the wheel of Dharma turned by the Tathāgata.
World-Honored One!
If a person can attain this Dharma-gate, that person is said to have attained the most supreme and wondrous Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Dharma-gate spoken by the Devaputra Sucintita,
saying: "Excellent, excellent, Devaputra!"
"So it is, so it is, just as you have said,
O Devaputra!
The treasury of the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is entirely contained within this Dharma-gate."
"O Son of Heaven!
All the intentions of all Buddhas have already been revealed within this Dharma-gate.
O Son of Heaven!"
If there are people who hear this Dharma-gate, you should know that these bodhisattvas have quickly obtained excellent benefit.
O Son of Heaven!
If there are people who hold this Dharma-gate in their hands, you should know that these bodhisattvas have attained the great treasury of the Dharma.
"O Son of Heaven!

If there is a person who upholds this Dharma-gate, you should know that such a bodhisattva is called one who is trustworthy; one who receives and maintains the secret treasury of the Tathāgata; one who honors the Tathāgata with the most supreme offerings; and one who embraces the Dharma-gate of the Tathāgata."
"O Son of Heaven!
If there is a person who hears this Dharma-gate and, having heard it, is able to believe it, you should know that such a bodhisattva is said to be repaying the kindness of the Tathāgata.
O Son of Heaven!"
"If there are those who believe in this Dharma-gate, you should know that these bodhisattvas will have no darkness or obstruction throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the entire great assembly, proclaiming these words:
"Who among you is able to protect and uphold this Dharma-gate in future ages?"
At that time, the Bodhisattva Anutpāda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!
"I shall be able to protect and uphold this Dharma-gate in future ages.
World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva has any [self-]arrogance, they will be unable to protect and uphold this Dharma."

Therefore, by not initiating, not arising, and not grasping, I am able to protect and uphold this profound Dharma-door of the patience regarding the non-arising of all phenomena with a mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings.
I have distanced myself from thoughts of food and drink, and I do not seek any offerings, honor, or praise. Why is this?
World-Honored One!
"World-Honored One, those who rely on offerings and veneration will be unable to protect and uphold this Dharma.

After the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, if there are those who hear this Dharma and are able to receive it, uphold it, transcribe it, read and recite it, or having transcribed it, even receive and uphold the physical volume— it should be known that all such instances are due to the majestic spiritual power of the Bodhisattva Aprodu."
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Asaṃprasthita, saying:
“Excellent, excellent! Son of good family!”
"If there are those who possess such a mind, these people will be able to protect and uphold the sublime Dharma.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva said,
"World-Honored One!"
If a person does not sever great compassion, that person is able to protect and uphold the sublime Dharma.
Therefore, I now rely upon the mind of great compassion to protect and uphold this Dharma-gate.
Maitreya Bodhisattva said:
“World-Honored One!
If a person possesses a mind of great compassion, that person is able to receive and uphold the sublime Dharma.”
Why is this? If a person is full of anger and hatred, that person cannot receive and uphold the sublime Dharma.
Therefore, I rely upon a mind of loving-kindness to circulate this Dharma-gate.
The Bodhisattva Lover of Those Who See said:
“World-Honored One!
If sentient beings never tire of seeing a bodhisattva, such a person is able to protect and uphold the sublime Dharma.”
“World-Honored One!
For this reason, I shall not give rise to a mind of anger toward any sentient being, and I shall protect and uphold this Dharma-gate.
Thus spoke the Bodhisattva Master (Nāyaka).
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva gives rise to the thought for the sake of all sentient beings:
‘I shall uproot the suffering of all sentient beings.’”
"If all sentient beings wish to gather the Buddha's bodhi and wish to deliver all sentient beings, this bodhisattva is able to receive and uphold this dharma-gate."
Therefore, World-Honored One,
I shall bring all sentient beings to the realization of Buddhahood.
World-Honored One!

"I shall first deliver all sentient beings and only then deliver myself; yet I do not perceive one who can deliver, nor one who is to be delivered, nor do I perceive the dharma by which sentient beings are delivered.
For this reason, World-Honored One!"
"I shall ultimately give rise to such a mind as this to protect and uphold this Dharma-gate.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva said,
"World-Honored One!"
People of the world are deluded; if a person gives rise to such a thought as,
"I shall protect and uphold the sublime Dharma," that itself is a delusion.
Why is this? World-Honored One!
A bodhisattva disciplines and pacifies their own body; this very dharma-body of the bodhisattva, being self-disciplined and self-pacified, is itself the upholding of the sublime Dharma.
"Therefore, World-Honored One!
My own body is supple, my own body is tranquil, and my own Dharma-body shall protect and uphold the sublime Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised that Bodhisattva who protects and upholds the sublime Dharma, saying:
“Excellent, excellent! Son of good family,
you are truly a great being (mahāsattva).”
Because you are now able to bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, you uphold the sublime Dharma.
A Bodhisattva who protects the Dharma ought indeed to act in this way. Why is that?
This is the most sublime and supreme activity of all bodhisattvas, namely, the upholding and protection of the sublime Dharma.
Son of good family!

This is the dharma-gate of the collection of dharmas corresponding to all dharmas; if a bodhisattva receives, upholds, recites, and practices it, that bodhisattva will obtain the manifestation of light from all Buddhas, and the bodies of all Buddhas will be seen as neither arising nor ceasing.
Within the Dharma, one attains the manifestation of great illumination, knowing that all phenomena are neither created nor conditioned;
within the Saṅgha, one attains the manifestation of illumination, realizing that the Saṅgha of the Tathāgata’s disciples is without self or what belongs to a self;
and through the Bodhisattva’s cultivation of the precepts, one attains the manifestation of illumination, wherein for the Bodhisattva among all trainings, great compassion is the root.
One attains the manifestation of the light of eloquence, wherein all speech and eloquence have non-arising as their essence. Good son!

This Dharma-gate circulates extensively in the world of the Naga King Sāgara, circulates extensively in the abode of Śakra, and circulates extensively in the abode of the Naga King Anavatapta; only thereafter does it circulate within Jambudvīpa.

Although he travels throughout Jambudvīpa, he always moves among those beings protected by the Buddhas, among those with straightforward minds free from deceit and crookedness, and among those capable of believing in the profound Dharma; he is always present within the hearts and hands of such beings.

When the Tathāgata preached this Dharma-gate, the Bodhisattva Asaṃprasthita, the Bodhisattva Vikrāntamati, and those other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as the great śrāvakas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and the entire great assembly, having heard this teaching of the Dharma-gate, rejoiced and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Collection of the Buddha’s Teachings, Scroll Six.
